    Lining up databases with the same tables#

    Keep one set of web and batch servers, line up many databases with the same tables as db.<name>, and choose the client's database for each request (2.7.8 completes the settings for this).

    • Good for: a database per client (or per group of clients); a dedicated database for a large client
    • Not for: hundreds of data sources or more. Pools, MQ claiming and the startup checks grow with the number of data sources. Aim for dozens at most (not one database per company)

    The shared database (the main one, main = true) holds the client ledger, the scheduler, batch management and so on; the shop databases hold the business tables and the MQ queue tables.

    Example configuration#

    # example of lined-up databases
db_templates {
	tenant {
		driver             = "org.mariadb.jdbc.Driver"
		username           = ${?SHOP_DB_USER}
		password           = ${?SHOP_DB_PASSWORD}
		maximum_pool_size  = 6
		minimum_idle       = 0              # do not keep connections open to idle databases
		connection_timeout = 3s             # do not let an unreachable database delay startup too much
		migration_dir      = "shop"         # the same SQL for every shop database
		migrate_on_startup = false          # apply from the CLI during deployment, not at startup
		codegen_name       = "shop"         # one set of generated code
		required           = false          # one going down does not stop startup or the health check
		framework_tables   = ["db_lock"]    # no framework tables the shop databases do not need
	}
}

db {
	startup_parallelism = 8                 # run the startup checks in parallel

	main {
		main     = true
		driver   = "org.mariadb.jdbc.Driver"
		url      = "jdbc:mariadb://db0/common"
		username = ${?DB_USER}
		password = ${?DB_PASSWORD}
		mq       = false                    # no queues on the shared database
	}

	shop_a = ${db_templates.tenant} { url = "jdbc:mariadb://db1/shop_a" }
	shop_b = ${db_templates.tenant} { url = "jdbc:mariadb://db1/shop_b" }
}

mq {
	hint           = redis                  # visit only the databases that have work
	sweep_interval = 10s
}

    Each setting is described in DB, Migrations and code generation and MQ. The template (db_templates) lives outside db { } and is copied and overridden with ${}.

    Choosing the database per request#

    In an entry filter, choose the database from the Host or the like and keep it on the request.

    before(context -> {
	String dataSource = tenants.dataSourceOf(context.request().host());   // look up the ledger (cached)
	if (dataSource == null) {
		throw new HttpException(404, "unknown host");
	}
	context.attribute(SHOP_DB, dataSource);
});

get("/orders", context -> {
	try (DB db = DBUtil.getDB(context.<String>attribute(SHOP_DB))) {
		context.response().json("orders", db.selectList(SQL.select().from(Order.instance())));
	}
});

    Careful

    Do not take the value that chooses the database from request parameters (query, form, JSON). Changing that value would hit another client's database. Derive it from something fixed by the route, such as the Host, and keep filtering by shop_id inside the shop database too.

    Keep the ledger (Host → data source name) in the shared database and cache the lookups (every request goes through it).

    What stays on the main data source#

    These live only on the main data source (the shop databases do not need them):

    • the scheduler (batch_master and the rest) and its MQ queue (mq_scheduler)
    • batch run records (batch_history and the rest); even a chunk batch running on a shop database records on the main one (Batch)
    • session and authentication tables (session, auth_*) and rate limits
    • code migrations (CodeMigration)

    Applying migrations#

    Set migrate_on_startup = false on the shop databases and apply them from the CLI during deployment.

    java -cp app.jar io.jimble.db.cli.JimbleDbCli migrate --migration-dir shop --parallel 4 --keep-going
java -cp app.jar io.jimble.db.cli.JimbleDbCli migrateCheck --migration-dir shop
# start the application once they line up

    A failure does not stop the others, and a per-data-source result is printed at the end. migrateCheck writes nothing and reports files not applied, extra records and hash mismatches per data source (Applying to databases lined up side by side).

    Generated code#

    With the same codegen_name, there is one set of generated code (the representative is the main data source, else the first by name). Table classes put only the table name into SQL, so run them with the database chosen for the request. Shop.db() returns the representative database, so do not use it for shop work (Sharing generated code).

    MQ#

    • Keep the queue table in the same database as the business tables, so enqueueing and the business update roll back together
    • Leave out databases that use no queues (such as the shared one) with mq = false. Putting to one that is left out throws
    • The poller orders the data sources by name and starts right after the one it last claimed from (one database with a backlog does not hold back the others)
    • With mq.hint = redis, only databases with work are visited. Every database is visited once per sweep_interval, which is the longest a row without a hint waits
    • Query estimate: with hint = off, even an idle process issues "queues × types × databases × 2 ÷ poll_max" SELECTs per second

    See "Choosing the data sources a queue lives on" and "Visiting only the databases that have work" in MQ.

    Connection counts#

    There is one pool per data source × write/read × parent and each sub.

    • Connections a process always keeps open = the sum of minimum_idle over those pools
    • Connections at peak = the sum of maximum_pool_size over those pools

    With 30 shop databases in the example above, the shop databases keep 0 open and reach 30 × 6 = 180 at peak (plus the main one). Set the database server's max_connections above the number of processes × the peak.

    SQL result cache#

    The SQL result cache is kept apart by data source name, so shop databases never share entries. For caches your application keeps itself (the ledger, settings, templates and so on), put the data source name into the key. Otherwise another client's value comes back.

    When one database goes down#

    Set required = false on the shop databases.

    • If one cannot be reached at startup, startup goes on, and once the database is back it just works
    • DBUtil.healthCheck() (the health check) looks only at required = true data sources, so one going down does not take the whole machine out of rotation
    • Per data source, use DBUtil.healthCheckAll()
    • A database that could not be reached at startup did not get its framework tables or migrations. Apply them with the CLI's migrate --data-source once it is back
    • MQ keeps going (since 2.7.9). A database that is down is retried after a pause (1 second, doubling up to 30 seconds), and meanwhile the other databases' rows keep being claimed. Once it is back, its rows are claimed again. Recovering stale rows and pendingCount() also skip the database that is down and return the others

    See DB.
